From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@heliodata.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity demo request — throughput details included

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick sign-up flow — we just finished our self-serve trial and it looks promising. We’re evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production inference path and would like a walkthrough focused on throughput and latency behavior for our workload. High-level requirements:

- Peak sustained QPS: ~300 requests/sec (in short bursts up to 600 for 2-3 minutes)
- Typical prompt + response token window: ~1k tokens (avg)
- Latency target: <= 120ms 95th-per-token for streaming use cases; 40–60ms preferred for internal benchmarks
- Model family: mainly decoder-only open models (chat-like prompts)

Can we set up a 30–45 minute demo next week? Prefer mornings PDT. I attached a one-pager with our load profile.

Also looping in Priya (engineering) who will join the call for deeper perf questions.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of ML Engineering, HelioData
alex.morgan@heliodata.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: helio_throughput_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Hi Alex — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the rundown and for the doc — that helps a lot.

Ben (SE) and I can cover this. Quick confirm items before we lock time:
- Is the 300 QPS steady-state across parallel session IDs, or do you consolidate into fewer sessions with larger batch sizes?
- Are you primarily concerned about per-token latency for streaming customers or end-to-end response latency?

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Wed 2026-05-20 10:00–10:45
- Wed 2026-05-20 11:30–12:15
- Thu 2026-05-21 09:00–09:45

If any of these work, I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short pre-call checklist so Ben can bring perf traces if needed. Also happy to shift to later if mornings don’t fit.

Best,

Thanks Rishi — Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PDT works for the team.

To answer: we run many short-lived sessions (hundreds of session ids); batch sizes are small on our side since we do per-user personalization. Latency is mostly per-token streaming latency — end-to-end response times are also important for user-facing features.

I'm attaching the doc (already sent) and a quick screenshot of our internal calendar for the 20th to confirm availability. Can you also confirm whether Redwood Dedicated supports automatic prefix/KV caching across sessions (we're trying to reduce per-token compute when users reuse prompts)?

Alex

Attachments: calendar-screenshot.png (PNG, 45KB)
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@heliodata.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 18:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity demo request — throughput details included

Alex / Priya — thanks for the details, that helps us tailor the demo. Short answers up front:
- Yes, Dedicated supports prefix/KV caching patterns and can be configured to cache across session ids for hot prefixes (depends on your privacy constraints).
- We can size a dedicated pool to handle 300 sustained QPS with short bursts; exact GPU counts depend on model family and quantization profile.

Couple of quick technical clarifications to prep the session (would save 10–15m on the call):
- Average sequence length (prompt + response) for your 1k token estimate — is that typically 400 tokens prompt + 600 tokens response?
- Are you using sampling or deterministic decoding (top-k/top-p) in production? Sampling affects throughput/latency predictability.
- Do you have any hard SLOs (e.g., 95th <= 120ms) that we should instrument for during the demo?

If you can drop answers in a quick reply, I’ll prepare a short benchmarking slide and a live perf run with a small test harness.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Pre-call asks (quick):
